title: Wireless microphone — input circuit
description: Reverse engineering the two-wire microphone front end of a JieLi AC7006-family wireless mic. The speaker endpoint is the ON M45 AUX input.

schematics.title: Mic input — observed connections
schematics.description: Continuity results as measured with the battery disconnected. Unknown values and unidentified nodes are deliberately retained.

schematics.title: U1 JL chip — physical contacts
schematics.description: A provisional U1 QFN-like symbol and physical pad map. The 20-contact estimate is based on photos, not a verified package datasheet. Pad labels describe positions, not manufacturer pin numbers.

schematics.title: AC-coupling — simulation sandbox
schematics.description: A generic source → capacitor → resistor filter for practicing CircuitJS1 editing and simulation. Not a reconstruction of the AC7006 input circuit.
assumptions: 1 kHz sine source at 50 mV peak
No microphone bias circuit or JL SoC internal model
Does NOT implement the five observed board parts as a verified circuit

STEP-004: With the microphone battery disconnected, confirm U1's physical contact count and orientation; do not assume a manufacturer pin-1 location.
Locate which physical U1 contact has continuity with C1R.2 (currently named JL-A); log contact side/position and nearby vias/capacitors.
Trace the previously unknown side of C1L. Record positive continuity, resistance values, no-continuity results, and the ground reference.
Update the measured netlist only after continuity confirms a connection. Do not assign official AC7006 pin functions from the 32-pin variant datasheet.
